rationale: The Latin anchors *contusio* (bruise/contusion) and *impressio* (impression/imprint) strongly point to a physical, visible mark made on a surface — i.e., a dent, blow-mark, or bruise — which aligns with mark.n.04 ("a visible indication made on a surface"). The sense of *sonus* (sound/blow) further supports a concrete physical impact sense, consistent with DYNT meaning a stroke or dent rather than any symbolic or metaphorical sense of "mark."
